bodies.intuition: Some capabilities appear to switch on abruptly with scale: flat at chance across several model sizes, then suddenly working. That claim shaped a great deal of thinking about what scaling buys. It is also disputed — the sharpness may be an artefact of grading answers as right or wrong rather than of anything happening inside the model.
bodies.engineer: The original observation was that certain benchmarks stay at random until a threshold and then rise steeply. The rebuttal is that those benchmarks use discontinuous metrics — exact match, multiple choice — and that swapping to a continuous one turns the same runs into smooth curves. Both readings fit the same data, which is why this entry cites both.
bodies.math: Under exact match, a task requiring L correct tokens scores p^L for per-token accuracy p, so smooth improvement in p looks like a threshold in p^L. The metric manufactures the discontinuity. Whether anything discontinuous also happens in the model is a separate question the metric cannot answer.
